html:
The Ten Years' War was the first Cuban war for independence from Spain, from 1868 to 1878. It began on 10 October 1868, when the planter Carlos Manuel de Cespedes freed his slaves at his estate of La Demajagua and called them to fight.

The rebels held the east of the island but never took the rich sugar west. Leaders such as Maximo Gomez and Antonio Maceo made their names. About two hundred thousand people died, many of disease.

The war ended in the Pact of Zanjon, which promised reforms but not independence; Maceo rejected it. It freed many slaves who had fought, and Spain abolished slavery in stages, ending it in 1886. The struggle resumed in the War of Independence of 1895, led by Jose Marti.
